context:
Goal: a red job wakes the batch runner at once (r50).
Problem (rule): PR #2860 needs `pull-requests: write` on 31 CI jobs in checks.yml and a run-end comment; your ruling R50 (12:14 CST Nov 12, page item 559 pick c) names neither. The stake is a rule: the permissions that CI jobs hold.
Based on (ruling): R50, roadmap/rulings/r50.json. Based on (read): PR #2860, head abdbab2563b9; the 31-job count comes from the coordinator and runner 10 (unmeasured by triage).
Departs from: main — jobs hold read-only pull-request permission (unverified by triage) — the PR gives 31 jobs write.
Cost of (c), from the lane's line counts, not measured: a poster job wired with needs: fires only after the last job ends, which ci-done already does. To wake on the first red job it must start with the run and poll the job list, so the delay is the poll interval, not at once. About 8 files, about 150 lines added and 350 removed; checks.yml loses 31 wake steps and 31 permission blocks and gains one wake-poster job; actions/ci-done-comment gets a polling mode; tests rewritten. One extra ubuntu runner is held for the whole CI duration on every ready PR run (minutes unmeasured). The lane's read: keeping per-job write with the two skip jobs exempt (push-skip and nightly-skip run only on push or schedule; push-skip keeps read) is the smaller change. A workflow-level pull-requests: write is wider, so it is not an option.
